Created one dropdown field (id 106131, dataset id 31319) with exactly 3 options (ProbeOptA/B/C) scoped to only the pool project (379335744 / PR-2005), then read it back via get_project_id_custom_fields_v2_v1 (project_id=379335744). The new field's `custom_fields[].option_values` array for id 106131 contains EXACTLY 3 rows — one per option, no duplicates:
  - {id:146665, option_value:'ProbeOptA', is_default:true, record_status:'active', dataset_id:31319}
  - {id:146666, option_value:'ProbeOptB', is_default:false, record_status:'active', dataset_id:31319}

Three distinct sequential option ids, three distinct values, no id-range doubling of any kind. This directly answers the open question: freshly created options are returned EXACTLY ONCE. The duplication seen on priority (8/4), status (10/5) and case_type (22/11) is therefore HISTORICAL DATA specific to those old default-field option sets, NOT a serializer artifact — a serializer bug would have doubled this brand-new field's options too, and it did not.
Bonus finding: these fresh custom-field option_values carry a `record_status` field (value 'active') plus `created_at`/`updated_at`/`dataset_id` — a discriminator that IS present here, on custom-field option rows, even though the prior probe of get_test_runs_form_fields_v1 found no discriminator (entity_type/record_status/count/is_active) anywhere. But this doesn't resolve the default_fields case: this same get_project_id_custom_fields_v2_v1 response's `default_fields.priority/status/case_type[].values` rows (re-observed in this same call, still duplicated 8/4, 10/5, 22/11 exactly as previously recorded) carry NO record_status field at all — only custom_fields rows get it. So record_status exists as a live column for custom-field options but is not surfaced (or does not exist) for the system default-field option rows, meaning it still cannot be used to pick a canonical id among the old duplicated defaults; it only confirms per-row lifecycle tracking exists at the custom-field-option level.
